headline: High risk of cascading misuse and capability conflict: Goose can write/egress broadly while social-auto-upload can push content to external platforms, creating unsafe default handoff paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, while social-auto-upload consumes local media/account files and uploads content. A shared filesystem bridge exists, so malicious or malformed content from one can influence the other if files are exchanged. No direct parser proof is present, so medium is the higher safe choice.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange files through the shared filesystem, prompt-like content in those files can be ingested by the other agent.
IF Goose is configured to read instructions from workspace files, injected instructions can affect its tool use.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic file ingestion for Goose.
Require manual review of any file passed between agents.
Use a read-only handoff directory.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress; social-auto-upload handles account data and media and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from Goose into upload workflows or external APIs. The pair is not proven to leak by default, but the shared filesystem makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace, files touched by Goose can be exposed to social-auto-upload.
IF social-auto-upload uploads a file that Goose placed in the shared directory, source code or secrets may leave the machine.
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts.
Restrict social-auto-upload to a curated upload folder.
Remove secrets from shared workspaces.
Audit outbound destinations before runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state; social-auto-upload can also write files in its account-file workflow and has broad network egress. The shared-state-via-filesystem model means concurrent runs can overwrite each other's artifacts, and Goose's git writes can be corrupted by parallel file operations. This is a default conflict pathway, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents run concurrently against the same directory, file overwrites or stale reads can occur.
IF Goose modifies git state while social-auto-upload writes adjacent files, repository state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Run only one agent per workspace.
Lock the repository before Goose writes.
Keep social-auto-upload in a separate account-file directory.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs.
requires-engineering: add cross-agent locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, edits, or operational outputs that social-auto-upload may treat as inputs for publishing. Because social-auto-upload has outbound API behavior and no verification mechanism is documented, erroneous or malicious Goose output can cascade into external posting or account actions. That makes the downstream blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Goose writes content that social-auto-upload later uploads, unverified errors can be published externally.
IF social-auto-upload is pointed at Goose-generated media or metadata, those artifacts can be acted on without review.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before upload.
Validate Goose outputs against a schema.
Use a staging account for test uploads.
Keep generated artifacts in a quarantine folder.
requires-engineering: add content-signing and verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to third-party platforms. If account data or secrets are placed in the shared workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two tools. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF account data or secrets are stored in the shared workspace, both tools may retain or transmit them under different policies.
IF the upload target has stricter retention or residency rules than Goose's local workspace, a compliance mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Use separate retention policies per tool.
Review upload platform terms before runs.
Purge temporary files after each session.
requires-engineering: document data-flow and retention controls.
